root_cause.text: symlink_data() in fs/smb/client/smb2file.c advanced through smb2_error_context_rsp entries using an unchecked, attacker-controlled ErrorDataLength, allowing 32-bit pointer arithmetic wraparound so the next context pointer could move backward or stay unchanged, causing an infinite loop or out-of-bounds read.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (len > end - ((u8 *)p + sizeof(*p))) return ERR_PTR(-EINVAL);` immediately before `p = (struct smb2_error_context_rsp *)(p->ErrorContextData + len);`, and the CVE/commit explicitly shows 32-bit cases where `ErrorDataLength` values like `0xfffffff8` make `next == p` and `0xfffffff0` make `next == (u8 *)p - 8`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a bounds check in symlink_data() to reject oversized SMB2 error-context lengths and prevent out-of-bounds parsing.
intent_record.what: A bounds check was added after computing the aligned error-context data length in symlink_data(): if len exceeds the remaining bytes between the current smb2_error_context_rsp payload start and end, the function now returns ERR_PTR(-EINVAL) before advancing p.
intent_record.how: This prevents the parser from moving p past the end of the SMB2 error buffer when ErrorDataLength is malformed or oversized, avoiding out-of-bounds access and rejecting invalid response data with -EINVAL.
